# Custom style recipes

A recipe is JSON: `"version": 1` and any of the blocks below. A block that is absent is off; a block that is present needs every value in it. The ranges are enforced (out of range is an error, not a clamp) and are the ones in `voice_capabilities` `sampleStyles.recipeLimits`. Nothing but numbers and the fixed choices below ever reaches the audio chain. Signal order is fixed: wobble, band, tone, squash, drive, crush, then room, then the beds underneath. Final loudness is levelled to about -18 LUFS.

## The blocks

| Block | Values (range) | What it does | Typical |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `band` | `lowCutHz` 40 to 600, `highCutHz` 2500 to 16000 | Cuts the lows and the highs: a thinner, smaller device. Raise `lowCutHz` to thin it, lower `highCutHz` to dull it. | phone or comms 285 to 350 low, 3000 to 3600 high; radio 220 and 4200; warm tape 45 and 7200 |
| `tone` | `warmthDb` -6 to 6 at 180 Hz, `presenceDb` -6 to 6 at 1.8 kHz | A low shelf for body and a mid bump for honk or edge. Positive presence sounds boxier, negative recedes. | presence 4 to 5 for phone or comms; warmth 2 to 2.5 for tape or vinyl |
| `drive` | `amountDb` 0 to 12 | Tube-like saturation: harder, more distorted. | 3 to 6; radio 12 |
| `crush` | `bits` 6 to 16 | Codec grain. Fewer bits is grittier; 16 is nearly clean. | 8 to 10 |
| `squash` | `ratio` 1 to 8 | Compression: evens the voice and makes it more pressed. | 2.5 for tape, 4.5 to 8 for phone or comms |
| `wobble` | `slowDepth` 0 to 1 (wow), `fastDepth` 0 to 1 (flutter) | Pitch drift: slow sway like a warped record, fast shimmer like tape. Both 0 adds nothing. | slow 0.3 to 0.7, fast 0 to 0.6 |
| `room` | `decaySeconds` 0.1 to 1.5, `brightHz` 1000 to 10000, `wetDb` 0 to 24 | A synthesized room: how long it rings, how bright the tail is, how much of it is heard. Higher `wetDb` is more room. | small room 0.3 to 0.4 s; hall 0.9; canyon 1.2 to 1.5; `wetDb` 9 to 19 |
| `beds` | up to 3, one of each kind, `levelDb` -60 to -20 | Sounds under the voice, each at most `levelDb` under it. See below. | |

Beds (`levelDb` is a ceiling, reached at the widest hiss band and the fastest crackle rate; a narrower hiss or slower crackle at the same value is quieter):

- `{"kind": "hiss", "color": "white" | "pink" | "brown", "lowHz": 20 to 8000, "highHz": 500 to 16000, "levelDb": ...}`: noise in a band, `lowHz` below `highHz`. White is bright static, pink is softer, brown is a low rumble.
- `{"kind": "crackle", "ratePerSecond": 1 to 60, "levelDb": ...}`: record ticks and pops.
- `{"kind": "crowd", "levelDb": ...}`: a wordless murmur made from the voice itself.
- `{"kind": "clinks", "levelDb": ...}`: a few glass and cup clinks.

Typical bed levels: hiss -30 to -42, crackle -23 to -26, crowd -22 to -25, clinks -26 to -30.

The recipe has no pitch shift, ring modulator, chorus or echo-taps block: robot, mask and helmet-lowered voices are the built-in `masked` and `helmet` styles. The built-ins also keep hand-tuned chains, so a recipe that looks like one is only near it. To use one exactly, pass `style`, not a recipe.

## From words to blocks

| They say | Reach for |
| --- | --- |
| walkie-talkie, comms, intercom, phone | narrow `band` (350 and 3200), `tone.presenceDb` 4, `squash` 6, `drive` 6, `crush` 8 to 10, faint white `hiss` |
| canyon, cave, hall, church, echo | `room` `decaySeconds` 1.2 to 1.5, `wetDb` 12 to 19; keep `brightHz` 2500 to 4000 for a dull tail |
| booth, bathroom, small room | `room` `decaySeconds` 0.2 to 0.4 |
| through a wall, next room, far away, muffled | `highCutHz` 2500 to 3000, `lowCutHz` about 120, `tone.presenceDb` -3 to -6, a little `room`; a `crowd` bed for a party |
| tape, cassette, warped, wobbly | `wobble` slow 0.3 to 0.5, fast 0.4 to 0.6, `squash` 2.5, `tone.warmthDb` 2 to 3, high white `hiss` |
| dusty record, vinyl, old | `wobble.slowDepth` 0.5 to 0.7, `crackle` 14 to 20 per second, `tone.warmthDb` 2.5, `highCutHz` 9000 |
| gritty, crunchy, broken speaker | more `drive` (8 to 12), fewer `crush.bits` (6 to 8) |
| warm, soft | `tone.warmthDb` 2 to 3, `highCutHz` 6000 to 9000 |
| tinny, thin | `lowCutHz` 400 to 600, `tone.presenceDb` 3 to 5 |

## Worked recipes

Each of these decodes with `decodeVoiceStyleRecipe` and renders. Save one as `recipe.json` to try it from the CLI (`voyager speech style --path voice.wav --output out.wav --recipe recipe.json --preview-seconds 5 --json`), or pass the same object as `recipe` to `voice_style_preview`.

Walkie-talkie in a canyon: a narrow, pressed, gritty band, a long dull room, faint static.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "band": { "lowCutHz": 350, "highCutHz": 3200 },
  "tone": { "warmthDb": 0, "presenceDb": 4 },
  "squash": { "ratio": 6 },
  "drive": { "amountDb": 6 },
  "crush": { "bits": 9 },
  "room": { "decaySeconds": 1.2, "brightHz": 3000, "wetDb": 14 },
  "beds": [{ "kind": "hiss", "color": "white", "lowHz": 600, "highHz": 6000, "levelDb": -38 }]
}
```

Heard through a wall at a party: dull, a little room, a crowd and some glass clinks.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "band": { "lowCutHz": 120, "highCutHz": 2800 },
  "tone": { "warmthDb": 2, "presenceDb": -3 },
  "room": { "decaySeconds": 0.6, "brightHz": 2500, "wetDb": 12 },
  "beds": [
    { "kind": "crowd", "levelDb": -22 },
    { "kind": "clinks", "levelDb": -30 }
  ]
}
```

Worn answering-machine tape: wow and flutter, warm and dull, compressed, bright hiss.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "wobble": { "slowDepth": 0.4, "fastDepth": 0.5 },
  "band": { "lowCutHz": 90, "highCutHz": 6000 },
  "tone": { "warmthDb": 3, "presenceDb": -2 },
  "squash": { "ratio": 2.5 },
  "drive": { "amountDb": 3 },
  "beds": [{ "kind": "hiss", "color": "white", "lowHz": 3000, "highHz": 12000, "levelDb": -32 }]
}
```

Dusty record: slow sway, warm, a little saturation, surface ticks.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "wobble": { "slowDepth": 0.6, "fastDepth": 0 },
  "band": { "lowCutHz": 70, "highCutHz": 9000 },
  "tone": { "warmthDb": 2.5, "presenceDb": 0 },
  "drive": { "amountDb": 4 },
  "beds": [{ "kind": "crackle", "ratePerSecond": 18, "levelDb": -26 }]
}
```

## Nudging one thing

Change one value, preview, name the change, and let the ear compare. Keep a note of the last recipe the user liked, so "go back" is exact.

| They say | One change |
| --- | --- |
| more static, hiss | the hiss `levelDb` up by 3 (not past -20), or a wider `lowHz` to `highHz` band |
| narrower, more muffled | `highCutHz` down by about 500 (not under 2500), or `lowCutHz` up by about 50 |
| more echo, bigger space | `room.decaySeconds` up by 0.2, or `wetDb` up by 3 |
| grittier | `crush.bits` down by 1, or `drive.amountDb` up by 2 |
| more wobbly | `wobble.slowDepth` up by 0.1 |
| less of anything | the same step the other way, or remove the block |

For example, "narrower" on the canyon recipe changes only `"highCutHz": 3200` to `"highCutHz": 2700`.

Saved styles change the same way: `voice_style_save` with the style's `id` and the new `recipe`. Takes already made keep the recipe they were made with.

## Limits

Recipes: three beds, one of each kind; every value in its range; at least one effect on (a wobble with both depths 0 does not count). Saved styles: 20 per user, names 1 to 60 characters, unique ignoring case, no invisible characters; they live in `<VOYAGER_HOME>/voice/styles.json` on this computer. Previews cover the first 5 seconds of a whole clean take.

# Sample styles

Each style is a fixed chain of FFmpeg filters on the voice plus a noise bed FFmpeg synthesizes (nothing is bundled). The voice is levelled to about −18 LUFS before styling and the result is brought back to it, so styles compare at equal loudness. Output is mono 44.1 kHz `.wav`, 0.5 s longer than the source. The same input, style and intensity render the same bytes.

| Style | What is applied | Heavier intensity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `telephone` | compression and saturation, then a narrow band (low cut 200–380 Hz, high cut 4.2 down to 3 kHz as intensity rises), a presence bump, line hiss and faint crackle | narrower, grittier, more hiss |
| `cafe` | slightly dull voice in a small synthesized room, behind it murmur (band-limited noise shaken at speech rhythm), low room tone and occasional glass clinks | more room and louder chatter |
| `radio` | saturation, AM-like band (low cut 120–320 Hz, high cut 7 down to 3.8 kHz), mid bump, slow flutter, short spring echo, static and crackle | narrower, more flutter and static |
| `cassette` | rolled-off highs, warm low mids, slow wow and fast flutter, tape compression and saturation, hiss | more wobble, duller, more hiss |
| `vinyl` | warm and slightly muffled, slow turntable wobble, surface noise, ticks and the odd pop | duller, more wobble and crackle |
| `helmet` (Trooper) | the voice about 1.3 semitones lower with the pace kept, a plastic-shell comb (echoes 2.6 and 4.1 ms behind it), a narrow comms band (low cut about 320 Hz, high cut about 3.6 kHz) with a honk at 1.6 kHz, hard soft-clipping into a ratio-8 compressor, a faint line hiss, a key-up click and short noise burst laid over the first 0.14 s (no lead-in, so no word moves) and a squelch just after the voice ends (inside the half-second tail) | narrower, more muffled, harder-driven, a stronger comb |
| `masked` (Masked host) | pitched down about 5.7 semitones tape-style (the formants fall too) with the pace kept, a 48 Hz ring modulator blended in, a chorus, a compressor, a hall's echoes at 60, 130, 210 and 340 ms and the top rolled off at 9 kHz; no noise bed | deeper, more metallic, more echo |

Intensity runs 0.1 to 1 (default 0.7). Treat 0.4 as a hint, 0.7 as the sample sound, 1 as the limit. A heavy style on a quiet, close recording hides less than on a loud one; if words get lost, lower the intensity before changing the style.

What it cannot do: it does not change the words, add real recordings of a place, or make a different voice. A voice that is already noisy or reverberant does not need it. Clean the recording first ([voiceover](../../voiceover/SKILL.md)).

---
name: sample-voice
description: 'Make a voice sound like a found sample: phone call, cafe, old radio, cassette, vinyl, helmet comms, masked host, or a custom style to save and reuse. For lo-fi spoken samples. Not narration or cleanup (voiceover).'
applications:
  - id: ffmpeg
    role: primary
  - id: moda
    role: alternative
---

Sample styles are a local, free effect on a recording the user already has or a take [voiceover](../voiceover/SKILL.md) made: band limit, saturation, a small room and a synthesized noise bed, in seven fixed styles or a custom recipe you write from the user's description. It never changes the words or timing, never touches the source, and costs no credits. A full styled take needs any paid plan (Starter and up); previewing a style and saving custom styles cost nothing and need no plan of their own (Free has no managed takes, so there previews go through `voyager speech style --preview-seconds` on a file). You cannot hear; the user judges by ear.

## 1. Pick the route

- **A managed take** (a Voice panel production, `voice_*` tools): call `voice_capabilities` once and read `sampleStyles.access`, then `voice_style` on a whole, clean, selectable take (not a passage, never a styled take). It makes a new `styled` take beside the clean one, with the same words and timing (captions still work), 0.5 s longer for the room or tape tail. Wait for the attempt (it has no media job, so `voyager jobs wait` does not apply: read `voice_take` with the `attemptId` until it is `completed` or `failed`; a plan refusal can arrive there as `PLAN_REQUIRED`), then play the styled take's `audioAbsolutePath`. Restyling, or another style: call `voice_style` again with the **clean** take's id (`style.cleanTakeId`).
- **Try a style first, free**: `voice_style_preview` renders the first few seconds of a clean take in a built-in style, a saved `customStyleId` or an inline `recipe`, and returns `audioAbsolutePath`. It makes no take, needs no plan and costs nothing (Sample voice styles must be on, which they are unless the user turned them off).
- **A custom sound** the built-in styles do not cover ("a walkie-talkie in a canyon"): write a `recipe` and follow [section 3](#3-build-a-custom-style). Preview it first, say which values you set, and save it only when the user asks (`voice_style_save`; `voice_style_list` shows what is saved, `voice_style_delete` removes one). Everything here needs Sample voice styles on (the default); building, previewing and saving are free on every plan.
- **Any other audio** (the user's recording, a file, a voice from another tool): `voyager speech style --path IN --output OUT.wav --style cafe --intensity 0.7 --json`. The output is a new `.wav`; the source stays. Put it beside the source, named for the style (`voice-cafe.wav`). A custom style takes `--recipe recipe.json` or `--custom-style-id ID` in place of `--style`, and `--preview-seconds 5` renders only the start, free on every plan.

Both routes check the plan the same way. Read [styles](references/styles.md) for what each style does and the intensity values.

## 2. Choose the style from the user's words

| They say | Style |
| --- | --- |
| phone call, telephone, answering machine, intercom | `telephone` |
| cafe, in a room, ambient chatter, overheard, restaurant, lobby | `cafe` |
| old radio, broadcast, AM, wartime, vintage announcer | `radio` |
| cassette, tape, dictaphone, home recording, wobbly | `cassette` |
| vinyl, record, crackle, dusty, warm, old film or LP | `vinyl` |
| trooper, stormtrooper, helmet, walkie-talkie, comms, soldier, sci-fi, static with a squelch | `helmet` (shown as Trooper) |
| masked host, game host, robot, mask, voice changer, PA announcement, ominous, anonymous | `masked` (shown as Masked host) |

"Sounds like a sample", "vintage" or "lo-fi" with no place named is exploring: render two or three styles at the default intensity (0.7) as separate files, name each by what was applied, and let them choose. When they named a place, make that one and offer one alternative. Intensity: 0.4 a hint, 0.7 clearly a sample (default), 1 as degraded as it goes; lower for a lead phrase that must stay intelligible, higher for a texture under a busy mix. Change one thing per revision (style or intensity) so the ear can compare.

## 3. Build a custom style

Use it when the user describes a sound none of the seven styles is (or says "my own style"). The built-ins stay the right answer when one fits: "old radio" is `radio`, not a recipe. Read [recipes](references/recipes.md) for each block's range and what it does, the words-to-values table and worked recipes.

A recipe is `version: 1` plus up to eight blocks, each on only when present: `band`, `tone`, `drive`, `crush`, `squash`, `wobble`, `room` and `beds` (at most three, one each of `hiss`, `crackle`, `crowd`, `clinks`). Every value is a number inside a fixed range or a fixed choice, so a value out of range is an error you fix, never a silent clamp. Take the ranges from `voice_capabilities` `sampleStyles.recipeLimits`. A recipe has no intensity: its values are the intensity. Bed `levelDb` is a ceiling under the styled voice (-20 at the loudest), not an exact level; final loudness is brought back to about -18 LUFS either way.

1. **Write it.** Choose the blocks the words call for and leave the rest out. A "canyon" is `room` with a long decay; a "walkie-talkie" is a narrow `band` with `squash`, `drive`, `crush` and a little hiss. Two or three blocks beat eight. Say what the recipe cannot do: pitch changes, robot or ring-mod voices (that is `masked`) and real places or real recordings.
2. **Preview it.** `voice_style_preview` with the clean take's `takeId` and the `recipe` (first 5 seconds, free, no take made; a whole clean take only). Hand over `audioAbsolutePath`, list the values you set ("band 350 Hz to 3.2 kHz, room 1.2 s decay, hiss at -38 dB") and ask the user to listen. Never say how it sounds.
3. **Adjust.** One change per revision so the ear can compare: "more static" raises the hiss `levelDb` by 3, "narrower" lowers `highCutHz` by about 500, "more echo" adds 0.2 s of `decaySeconds` or 3 to `wetDb`. Preview again each time and name the change.
4. **Save only when asked.** Once they like it, offer to keep it. On a yes, `voice_style_save` with a `name` (1 to 60 characters, unique for this user, ignoring case; no invisible characters) and the recipe. To change a saved style, pass its `id` with a new `name`, a new `recipe` or both. Saved styles are per user, across every project, at most 20 (ask which to delete when full). Saving is free; never save unasked.
5. **Apply it.** `voice_style` on the whole clean take with the `recipe` or, for a saved style, its `customStyleId` from `voice_style_list` or `sampleStyles.savedStyles`. Exactly one of `style`, `customStyleId` or `recipe`; `intensity` only goes with a built-in `style`. A full take needs any paid plan, Starter and up ([section 5](#5-plans-and-refusals)). The take keeps its own copy of the recipe, so renaming, editing or deleting the saved style never changes it; to use the edited style, run `voice_style` again on the clean take.

Custom styles render through FFmpeg only. Re-rendering the same recipe on the same take gives the same bytes. An older Voyager build cannot read a production that holds a custom take, so mention it before the user opens such a project on one.

Without a managed take, the CLI does the same on any audio file: `voyager speech style --path voice.wav --output voice-walkie.wav --recipe recipe.json --preview-seconds 5 --json` to hear it, `voyager speech style-save --name "Walkie-canyon" --recipe recipe.json --json` to keep it, `voyager speech style-list --json`, `voyager speech style --path voice.wav --output voice-walkie.wav --custom-style-id vstyle_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --json` to use it and `voyager speech style-delete --id vstyle_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --json`. A recipe file is plain JSON with plain numbers.

## 4. Fit it to music

A sample is a short phrase, not a paragraph, and it sits low and filtered under the track. Cut the voice to the phrase first (before styling, on the clean take: [speech edits](../edit-video/SKILL.md#speech-edits)), style the phrase, then place and level it in the mix as [make-sound](../make-sound/SKILL.md#mix-to-the-destination) describes. Do not invent mixing rules here: duck, level and deliver as make-sound does. Style once, after the cut: a cut of a styled file cuts its tail.

## 5. Plans and refusals

- `sampleStyles.access` `off`, a tool error `sample_styles_off` or a CLI `INVALID_INPUT` with that `details.reason`: the user turned Sample voice styles off. This is checked before the plan. Tell the user in one line to turn Sample voice styles back on in Settings → Creative, then try again; there is nothing to preview, save or list until then, and do not fake the effect another way. `settings_unreadable` (CLI, retryable): try again in a moment.
- `sampleStyles.access` `included`: go ahead. `unknown`: the plan is not known yet; call `voice_style` or the CLI and let the result decide.
- `upgrade_required`, a `PLAN_REQUIRED` error with reason `ultra_required`, or a CLI `QUOTA` error with `details.reason` `ultra_required`: say in one line that a full styled take comes with any paid plan (Starter and up) and give the link from the error (the clean file is unchanged and usable). Do not offer `voice_style` (`voice_style_preview` and saved styles still work), and do not fake the effect with your own FFmpeg chain or another provider unless the user asks you to.
- `INVALID` `already_styled`: style the clean take. `not_a_whole_take`: choose a full, assembled, edited or converted take. `not_a_clean_take` (a preview): preview on a whole clean take, never a passage, audition, preview or styled take.
- `invalid_recipe` (CLI `INVALID_INPUT`): the message names the value and its path ("Expected a value between 40 and 600 at band.lowCutHz"). Fix that field and preview again; a recipe is never clamped. Also refused: an unknown block or field, a block missing one of its values, more than three beds or two of one kind, a hiss with `lowHz` not below `highHz`, and a recipe with no effect on.
- `invalid_style_name`, `duplicate_style_name` (ask for another name, or change that style by `id`), `style_limit` (20 saved: ask which to delete), `style_not_found` (the style was deleted: `voice_style_list`), `style_choice` (give exactly one of `style`, `customStyleId`, `recipe`), `style_library_busy` (retry in a few seconds), `style_library_unreadable` (tell the user; pass the recipe inline meanwhile). A `warning` on `voice_style_list` means some saved styles could not be read by this version; they are kept unchanged, so pass the warning on.
- The CLI's full `speech style` (not `--preview-seconds`) also needs Voyager sign-in: signed out it fails `AUTH_REQUIRED`.
- A user who says they just upgraded: try once; the check asks the account live.

## 6. Report honestly

Say what was applied ("Cafe at 0.7: band-limited, small room, murmur and clinks underneath"), never that it sounds like a cafe or sounds good. Give the paths of both files (clean and styled), say the clean one is unchanged, and offer a different style or intensity. Never approve a styled take for the user unless they delegated approval.
